code: library(NHSOFearlystagecancer)  example_df <- data.frame(   date = rep(as.Date("2026-02-01"), 5),   org_code = rep("ABC", 5),   deprivation = c("1 - most deprived", "2", "3", "4", "5 - least deprived"),   ed_prop = c(0.55, 0.58, 0.595, 0.606, 0.619),   ed_denom = c(39546, 43663, 48796, 51117, 50739) )  knitr::kable(example_df) example_result <- example_df |>    derive_sii(     by = c("date", "org_code"),     ed_prop_col = "ed_prop",     ed_denom_col = "ed_denom",     depr_col = "deprivation" )  example_result[, c("org_code", "sii")] #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   org_code    sii #>   <chr>     <dbl> #> 1 ABC      0.0804 example_result <- score_sii(example_result, by = "date")  example_result[, c("org_code", "sii", "sii_score")] #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   org_code    sii sii_score #>   <chr>     <dbl>     <int> #> 1 ABC      0.0804         3

title: Create Slope Index of Inequality (SII) for Deprivation Gap metric — derive_sii
text: calculations done follows: Scale deprivation quintile groups 0 1. quintile assigned midpoint proportion population represents. example, first 20%, quintile 1, placed 0.1 (10%) Compute inverse variance binomial proportion use weighting subgroup. deprivation quintile , weighting \(w_i\) calculated early diagnosis proportion \(p_i\), count staged cases \(n_i\) : $$w_i = \frac{n_i}{p_i(1 - p_i)}$$ Note reason early diagnosis required proportion 0 1 flow calculating weighting. Build weighted linear regression models group specified , applying helper function fit_sii(). linear model uses scaled deprivation quintile predicting early diagnosis proportion, weighted inverse variance. Take SII coefficient scaled deprivation quintiles. , scaling 0 1, gradient slope gives us entire deprivation gap.

title: Fits an individual SII model — fit_sii
text: Fit line form $$   y = \alpha + \beta x_i + \epsilon_i $$ minimises: $$\sum{weights * \epsilon^2}$$ SII taken \(\beta\). fully given expected inputs: $$  \text{Early Diagnosis %} = \text{Intercept} + \text{SII} * \text{Scaled  Deprivation} + \text{Error} $$
